raw_response:
I am old now, I do not read books, so I farm by what I have seen on my own land and what people around me do. On 12 mu I will not make big changes. Wheat and maize are still my main safe way, because one follows the other and we always have grain income. Cotton I will keep on a smaller piece, because if the year is good it brings cash, but it takes more picking work and my family only has 2 people. I have a well, so if it turns dry I can still save the crop, but pumping water costs money, so I will not water too many times unless I see the soil really drying or the crop looking weak. For wheat, I will sow in early October like usual, use the seed people nearby use, put a good base fertilizer and then add some more when the wheat starts growing strong in spring. After wheat harvest in June, I will plant maize quickly on the same land, because the turnaround is short and there is no time to do fancy work. Cotton I will plant in April on the smaller piece, use a moderate amount of fertilizer, and watch insects carefully because cotton can lose badly if pests get ahead. I would rather spend a bit on enough fertilizer and one or two sprays than let the field go weak and lose yield.
